description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a beloved Hong Kong bakery classic featuring a soft, sweet bread base topped with a crispy, crumbly, sugary crust. Despite their name, these golden-domed delights contain no pineapple; their moniker comes from the signature cracked appearance of the topping, resembling a pineapple's skin. Enjoy them fresh from the oven, perhaps with a slice of butter tucked inside, for an unforgettable taste of Cantonese comfort.

or regular milk, for pineapple topping

instructions.title: Prepare the Bun Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine bread flour, 30g granulated sugar, instant dry yeast, and salt. Make a well in the center and pour in the warm milk and beaten egg. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Transfer to a lightly floured surface and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Gradually add the softened butter and continue kneading for another 5-7 minutes until the butter is fully incorporated and the dough passes the windowpane test.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Place the kneaded dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until doubled in size. This is the first fermentation.

instructions.title: Make the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is proofing, prepare the topping. In a medium bowl, cream together the softened 50g unsalted butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk, evaporated milk, and vanilla extract (if using). In a separate bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, milk powder (if using), and baking powder. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, mixing until just combined and a soft, pliable dough forms. Do not overmix. Cover and chill in the refrigerator.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns and Apply Topping
instructions.text: Once the dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release the air. Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Take the chilled topping dough and divide it into 8 equal portions. Flatten each topping portion into a disc large enough to cover about two-thirds of the bun. Gently place a topping disc over each bun, pressing lightly to adhere. You can use a dough scraper to create a pineapple-like crisscross pattern on the topping if desired.

instructions.title: Second Proofing and Egg Wash
instructions.text: Arrange the shaped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let them rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. While they are proofing, preheat your oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit). Just before baking, gently brush the topping of each bun with the egg wash (egg yolk mixed with water).

instructions.title: Bake the Pineapple Buns
instructions.text: Bake the pineapple buns in the preheated oven for 18-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and cracked, and the buns are cooked through. The internal temperature of the bun should reach 90 degrees Celsius (195 degrees Fahrenheit). Transfer the baked buns to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving. For an authentic experience, serve warm, perhaps with a slice of cold butter tucked inside.

tips: To achieve the perfect pineapple crust, ensure your topping dough is well-chilled before shaping and applying. This helps it hold its shape and crack beautifully during baking.
For an extra rich flavor and softer crumb in the bun dough, consider replacing 1-2 tablespoons of milk with heavy cream.

Pineapple buns are best enjoyed fresh on the day they are baked. If you have leftovers, store them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. Reheat briefly in a toaster oven for best results.
article:
Mastering the Art of Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao (Chinese Baking)

There are few pastries as iconic and beloved in Chinese bakeries as the Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao. With its distinctive crunchy, sweet topping reminiscent of a pineapple's skin (hence the name, despite containing no actual pineapple!), and its fluffy, soft bread underneath, it’s a delightful treat that captures hearts from Hong Kong to your very own kitchen. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that authentic bakery experience at home, you're in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to bake perfect Pineapple Buns, including a detailed Pineapple Bun recipe that will impress your family and friends. Get ready to embark on a delicious journey into the world of Chinese baking!

## What is Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao?
Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao (菠蘿包), is a sweet bun originating from Hong Kong, deeply ingrained in Cantonese cuisine. Its name is a charming misnomer; there's no pineapple fruit involved. Instead, the "pineapple" refers to the golden-brown, cracked, sugary crust that tops the bun, which visually resembles the rough exterior of a pineapple. This unique topping is typically made from a dough of sugar, eggs, flour, and butter, which bakes into a crisp, crumbly shell. Beneath this delightful crust lies a soft, slightly sweet yeasted bread roll, often enjoyed plain, with a slab of cold butter (known as "Bo Lo Yau"), or sometimes filled with custard, red bean paste, or even barbecued pork (char siu). It's a staple for breakfast, afternoon tea, or as a comforting snack, offering a wonderful contrast of textures and flavors in every bite.

## Ingredients You Need
Crafting the perfect Pineapple Bun requires two main components: the soft bread dough and the signature pineapple topping. Here’s a detailed list of ingredients for this authentic Pineapple Bun recipe.

For the Bread Dough:
*   3 cups (360g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
*   1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar
*   1 teaspoon instant dry yeast
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1/2 cup (120ml) warm milk (around 105-115°F / 40-46°C)
*   1 large egg, room temperature
*   1/4 cup (55g) unsalted butter, softened
*   1 tablespoon milk powder (optional, for extra softness)

For the Pineapple Topping:
*   1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened
*   1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
*   1 large egg yolk
*   1/4 teaspoon baking powder
*   1 1/2 cups (180g) all-purpose flour
*   1-2 tablespoons milk (if needed, to adjust consistency)

For Egg Wash:
*   1 large egg, beaten

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Follow these steps carefully to create your own batch of irresistible Pineapple Buns. This comprehensive Pineapple Bun recipe is designed for success!

1.  **Prepare the Bread Dough:**
    *   In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, yeast, salt, and milk powder (if using).
    *   In a separate bowl, combine warm milk and egg. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
    *   Add the softened butter and knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for 10-15 minutes, until it's smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test (you can stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing).
    *   Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

2.  **Prepare the Pineapple Topping:**
    *   While the dough is rising, cream together the softened butter and sugar in a medium bowl until light and fluffy.
    *   Beat in the egg yolk until well combined.
    *   Sift in the flour and baking powder, mixing until just combined to form a soft dough. If it's too crumbly, add milk 1 tablespoon at a time until it comes together. Do not overmix.
    *   Wrap the topping dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm up.

3.  **Shape the Buns:**
    *   Once the bread dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release the air.
    *   Divide the dough into 10-12 equal pieces (around 60-70g each).
    *   Roll each piece into a smooth ball. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between each.
    *   Cover the buns loosely with plastic wrap and let them proof again for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.

4.  **Apply the Topping:**
    *   Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
    *   Take the pineapple topping dough from the fridge. Divide it into the same number of pieces as your buns.
    *   Working with one piece at a time, roll it out between two sheets of parchment paper or plastic wrap into a thin circle, slightly larger than the top of your bun.
    *   Carefully peel off one side of the parchment/plastic and gently place the topping circle over a proofed bun. Gently press it down around the edges to adhere. Repeat for all buns.
    *   Using a knife or a dough scraper, gently score a cross-hatch pattern on the surface of the topping (optional, but adds to the classic look).

5.  **Bake the Buns:**
    *   Brush the exposed bread dough (around the sides of the topping) with the beaten egg wash. Avoid brushing the topping itself, as this can prevent it from cracking properly.
    *   Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and cracked, and the bread is cooked through.
    *   Transfer the baked buns to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
Achieving bakery-quality Pineapple Buns requires a little attention to detail. Here are some pro tips to perfect your Pineapple Bun recipe:

*   **Yeast Activation:** Ensure your milk is the correct temperature (105-115°F / 40-46°C) for activating yeast. Too hot will kill it, too cold won't activate it, leading to dense buns.
*   **Kneading is Key:** Don't skimp on kneading the bread dough. Proper gluten development is essential for a soft, airy crumb. The windowpane test is your best friend here.
*   **Proofing Environment:** A warm, draft-free place is ideal for dough rising. If your kitchen is cold, turn your oven on for a few minutes, then turn it off and let the dough rise inside with the door slightly ajar.
*   **Topping Consistency:** The pineapple topping dough should be pliable but not sticky. If it's too soft, add a little more flour; if too stiff, a tiny bit of milk. Chilling it makes it easier to handle and roll out thinly.
*   **Thin Topping:** Roll the topping as thinly as possible. A thin topping will crack more beautifully and provide a better texture contrast with the soft bun.
*   **Don't Overbake:** Keep an eye on the buns. Overbaking can dry out the bread. The topping should be golden, and the bread should sound hollow when tapped on the bottom.

## Serving Suggestions
Pineapple Buns are incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. For the most traditional experience, slice a warm bun horizontally and insert a thick slab of cold butter (Bo Lo Yau). The contrast of the warm, soft bun with the melting, salty butter is heavenly. They are also fantastic on their own with a cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea or coffee for breakfast or an afternoon snack. You can also get creative by adding fillings like sweet custard, red bean paste, or even savory char siu (BBQ pork) before baking for a more substantial meal.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Pineapple Bun is a masterpiece on its own, there are many ways to customize and adapt this Pineapple Bun recipe to your liking.

*   **Fillings:** As mentioned, adding fillings before the second proofing is popular. Sweet custard, red bean paste, or even a simple cream cheese filling can elevate the bun. For a savory twist, try char siu pork.
*   **Topping Flavors:** You can slightly adjust the topping's flavor profile. A pinch of vanilla extract or almond extract can add a subtle aromatic note. For a chocolate twist, incorporate a tablespoon of cocoa powder into the topping dough.
*   **Whole Wheat Flour:** For a slightly healthier (though less traditional) bread, you can substitute a small portion (up to 1/4) of the all-purpose flour with whole wheat flour. This will result in a denser bun.
*   **Dairy-Free:** For a dairy-free version, use plant-based milk (like almond or soy milk) and a dairy-free butter substitute for both the dough and the topping.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While challenging due to the need for gluten for the bread's structure, some specialized gluten-free flour blends may work for the bread dough, though results will vary. The topping can often be adapted more easily with gluten-free flour.

Baking Pineapple Buns at home is a rewarding experience that brings a taste of authentic Chinese bakery culture right to your kitchen. With this detailed Pineapple Bun recipe and our expert tips, you're well-equipped to create these beloved treats. Enjoy the process, savor the aroma, and delight in the incredible taste of your homemade Bo Lo Bao!
